prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures a downward-angled egocentric view over a grassy lawn, showing the camera wearer's own chest, beard, and shoulders at the bottom edge (0.1–0.3 m away, brightest white), their extended left arm and fist (0.4–0.7 m in front and to the left in frames 2–4), and their legs and feet below (1.0–1.5 m away, medium grey). A second person standing in front of the wearer enters at the top of frame 3 at roughly 3–4 m, approaches to about 1.5–2.0 m in frame 4 (where they hold a paper sheet within their own arm's reach on their right side, about 1.5 m from the wearer), and shifts to the left edge at 1.5–2.0 m in frame 5 as the wearer turns right. The depth map makes the continuous ground-plane distance gradient and the elevated height of the wearer's raised left arm above the turf much clearer than in the uniform green RGB grass. However, the map is unreliable along the dark vignette corners where the lawn falsely appears infinitely far, in frame 3 where the distant person's feet blend almost completely into the ground plane, and in frame 4 where the person's lower legs fade into the background depth.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's lower body and extended left arm at the bottom of all five frames (0.1–1.5 m away) and tracks the second person in front of the wearer across frames 3–5, whose upper torso and head remain cut off above the top frame boundary so their gaze direction is not visible. In frame 3, only the second person's feet are visible at the top center (~3–4 m ahead, facing toward the wearer); in frame 4, they are ~1.5–2.0 m ahead and slightly left, facing the wearer's left side with a white paper in their right hand; in frame 5, their bare legs and feet appear at the middle-left edge (~1.5–2.0 m away) below a separate top-left fragment as the wearer turns clockwise. Nothing external is within arm's reach of the camera wearer, whereas the clipboard/paper is held directly within the second person's right hand in frames 4–5. Compared to RGB, the masks clearly highlight the small foot regions at the top of frame 3 against the grass, but the map is unreliable when it splits the wearer's single left arm into two separate 'person' instances in frame 2, misses the held paper in frame 4 while misclassifying a small leaf/hole on the lawn in frame 1 (~1.8 m ahead) and the wearer's right knee in frame 4 (~1.2 m below) as 'sports ball', and fragments the person on the left in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, detecting only the camera wearer's raised left hand (magenta) and upper-body shoulder/neck joints (yellow) across frames 2–4 while leaving frames 1 and 5 completely blank. In frames 2 and 3, the magenta hand skeleton shows the wearer's left hand raised in a curled fist at roughly 0.5–0.6 m in front of and slightly left of the head, connected structurally above the yellow shoulder line at the bottom (0.1–0.3 m from the camera). In frame 4, as the wearer steps forward and begins turning right toward the approaching person (~1.5–2.0 m ahead), the left hand skeleton shifts rightward toward the center of the view and uncurls to point forward and right at ~0.5 m distance, while the yellow torso keypoints drop out. The magenta wireframe makes the exact finger articulation and transition from a closed fist (frames 2–3) to an extended index finger (frame 4) easier to read than in the foreshortened RGB view, though it is unreliable because it misses the wearer's lower body and right arm in frames 1 and 5, fails to detect the second person's legs, torso, or paper-holding hand in frames 3–5, and provides no information on the other person's facing or gaze direction.
